newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks hold modest gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks hold modest gains at close.

text.p: The Australian share market ended with modest gains on Monday with a rebounding Wall Street providing the inspiration.
However, early strength was sapped by a gold sector that dived 1.6 percent after the bullion price tumbled offshore.
The All Ordinaries index added 10.3 points to 2,409.8.
The bourse peaked early before CRA and WMC pulled it off its highs and by mid-morning it had found the four-point range in which it spent most of the day.
"It's been running on the back of New York and it is still relatively quiet," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co.
With a dearth of corporate news on the leaders, the medium size oil companies took centre stage with a combination of value-seeking investors and promising drilling results taking traders' interest.

Featuring early was First Australian Resources whose shares shot up after it reported strong oil and gas flows from its south Louisiana field in the U.S. Its shares closed 44 percent higher at A$0.375 (US$0.30).
Bligh Oil was also boosted by a U.S. drilling report from its first well in the Rainosek project in Texas, its shares ending up 28 percent at A$0.77.
Situation stock Highlands Gold went against the gold sector trend, its shares adding four cents to A$0.79 after it unveiled restructuring plans to fend off a hostile bid from gold major Placer Dome.
In the industrials, shares in retailer David Jones continued to slide after Friday's warning of a 50 percent cut in first half net profit because of depressed retail trading conditions.
Shares in the upmarket department operator closed seven percent lower at A$1.56.
Rises barely shaded falls, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
